title: Photophysics of atmospheric anions: photodissociation spectroscopy of CO 3 ˙ − (H 2 O) 1,2
content: Bare and hydrated carbonate radical anions, which are present in the lower region of the ionosphere, are among the most abundant negative molecular ions. Since photoinduced solvent evaporation affects the hydration state of these species, reliable cross sections for their interaction with light are essential for quantitative modelling of negative-ion chemistry in the atmosphere. In this study, we report experimental photodissociation spectra of CO3˙−(H2O)1,2 in an 85 K black-body radiation environment, obtained on a Fourier Transformation Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometer (FT-ICR-MS) equipped with a tuneable laser system. We observed water loss from CO3˙−(H2O)1,2 after one-photon absorption at ≈1.7–2.8 eV. The experimental data is compared to theoretical spectra based on path integral molecular dynamics with a coloured-noise thermostat for ground-state sampling. Multireference calculations are used to analyse excitation energies and dissociation pathways. We show that after excitation, the clusters relax on the sub-ps timescale to the first excited state through a series of conical intersections, converting most of the excitation energy to vibrational energy, which leads to the evaporation of the water molecules.
